source: Source: U.S. Dept. of Labor, "A Look at 401(k) Plan Fees"

scenes.text: Quick! Guess what one extra percent in fees can cost you over 35 years.
scenes.say: Quick! Guess what one extra percent in fees can cost you over thirty-five years.
scenes.head: GUESS THE NUMBER

scenes.text: The U.S. Department of Labor ran it: $25,000 in a 401(k), 35 years, 7% a year.
scenes.say: The U.S. Department of Labor ran it: twenty-five thousand dollars in a four-oh-one-k, thirty-five years, seven percent a year.
scenes.head: THE OFFICIAL EXAMPLE

scenes.text: Half a percent in fees leaves $227,000. One and a half leaves $163,000.
scenes.say: Half a percent in fees leaves two hundred twenty-seven thousand. One and a half leaves one hundred sixty-three thousand.
scenes.head: SAME MONEY. DIFFERENT FEE.

scenes.text: Did you guess it? Because if not, then...
scenes.head: DID YOU GUESS IT?
